_note: Elemental modifiers for ranged weapons. Taking one converts EVERY ranged weapon you own: the bullet it fires, the impact it leaves, and the lasting damage it does. One choice, visible everywhere, which is what makes it read as a build decision rather than another percentage.
_designNote: An element RECOLOURS each weapon's own round rather than replacing it. Every signature round is packed in three element colours, so a fire Scattergun still throws a burst and a fire Harpoon still throws a spear - both orange. Swapping the clip outright, which is what this used to do, made every weapon fire an identical bullet the moment you took an element, erasing the weapon identity the bullets exist to communicate.
_payloadNote: The lasting damage rides on the projectile payload fields the weapon riders already use (burnDps, bleedDps, slowOnHit, markPct, knockback) and is applied by World.applyHit, so an element needed no new damage plumbing at all.
_riderNote: docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md batch 1 took the Loads from three to nine, and the six new ones are not all damage-over-time. `chain*`, `hitHazard*`, `killHazard*` and `killHeal` are the LOAD'S OWN riders and they live here rather than on the item in items.json for one reason: a Load is exclusive -- taking one replaces the last -- but the ITEM stays in player.items forever. A rider read off the item would keep firing after its Load had been swapped away. World.refreshSpecialItems reads these off the ACTIVE element, so exactly one Load's riders are ever live. hitHazard rides H6's spawnHazard at the on-hit call site; killHazard rides it in killEnemy; chain is H1; killHeal is H11.
_artNote: The six new Loads ship with NO projectile colourway. renderer.ts falls back to the weapon's base clip when `proj.<clip>.<element>` was never packed, so a new Load is legible on day one and the recolour pass (npm run recolour over the 7 signature clips) is a follow-up rather than a blocker.
_retuneNote: Batch 1's Loads were authored in docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md SS6 and then MEASURED, and the six new ones came in under the three they compete with. A Load converts every ranged weapon you own, so it is the largest single multiplier in the game and a new one that is a downgrade is worse than no new one at all: the shop would be diluting its own best slot three to one. salt 22 -> 30, lime 12 -> 20, spark 0.45 -> 0.6, kerosene 10 -> 16 dps, font 3 -> 4 heal. The retune pass SS9 reserves for batch 5 starts here rather than there, because the harness would not have let it wait.
_stackNote: A `<field>PerStack` beside a base field is what a SECOND (or third) copy of the same Load adds on top of it, additive, read by `World.applyElementTo` and by `offers.ts`' `loadStatDelta` off the identical formula: value at stack N is `base + perStack * (N - 1)`. Only fire/acid/frost carry one today because they are the only Loads with `maxStacks > 1` in items.json -- the six batch-1 Loads are `maxStacks: 1` (`ONE ONLY`, per docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md's own table), so `N` can never exceed 1 for them and the formula is a no-op, not a special case. That is the 'one rule' Part 2 asked for: nothing here checks an item id, only whether a `PerStack` field exists. Before this, `Player.addItem` set `this.element` and stopped -- a second or third Tracer Rounds re-asserted 'fire' over itself and changed nothing, which is exactly the owner's 'what does buying fire 5 times do' complaint.

fire.name: Fire
fire._note: Burns, and sets slop slicks alight — a fire build turns the Chem Sprayer's puddle from a slow into a killing field.

acid.name: Acid
acid._note: Corrodes. Lower burst than fire, longer bite, and it stacks with the armour-shredding fantasy of the late waves.

frost.name: Frost
frost._note: No damage over time; it buys space instead. The one element that is defensive, so an element pick is not purely a damage race.

salt.name: Rock Salt
salt._note: No damage of its own at all. It opens the target up and lets everything ELSE you own do more — which is why it is the Load a heavy weapon build wants and the one a solo pistol build should not take.

lime.name: Quicklime
lime._note: Half of salt's mark and a slow with it. The compromise Load: a little of both, best of neither, and the one that makes Cross-Contamination trivial to satisfy on its own.

spark.name: Fence Charge
spark._note: H1. The only Load whose value scales with how PACKED the field is rather than with how long a target lives, so it is the answer to the late waves that fire and acid are not.

kerosene.name: Kerosene Load
kerosene._note: H6 at the on-hit site. Every hit leaves burning ground, so a fast weapon paints the field and a slow one does almost nothing with it — the first Load whose worth depends on which gun you are holding.

tar.name: Tar Load
tar._note: H6 at the kill site. Slows on hit and leaves a slick where things die, so a crowd killed in one place becomes ground the rest of the crowd cannot cross.

font.name: Font Water
font._note: The one Load with no damage-over-time and no mark. It buys SPACE on hit and HEALTH on kill, which makes it the defensive pick the way Frost is, without being Frost. Epic because a sustain source that scales with kill rate is the strongest thing the Load slot can hold.
